document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The King Dhritarashtra asked, "O Sanjaya! What happened on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra when my people and the Pandavas gathered?"

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The King Dhritarashtra asked, "O Sanjaya! What happened on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra when my people and the Pandavas gathered?"
metadata.sanskrit_text: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः। मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय।।1.1।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Sanjaya replied: "When Prince Duryodhana saw the Pandavas' army paraded, he approached his preceptor Guru Drona and spoke these words:

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Sanjaya replied: "When Prince Duryodhana saw the Pandavas' army paraded, he approached his preceptor Guru Drona and spoke these words:
metadata.sanskrit_text: सञ्जय उवाच दृष्ट्वा तु पाण्डवानीकं व्यूढं दुर्योधनस्तदा। आचार्यमुपसङ्गम्य राजा वचनमब्रवीत्।।1.2।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Revered Father! Behold this mighty host of the Pandavas, paraded by the son of King Drupada, your wise disciple.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Revered Father! Behold this mighty host of the Pandavas, paraded by the son of King Drupada, your wise disciple.
metadata.sanskrit_text: पश्यैतां पाण्डुपुत्राणामाचार्य महतीं चमूम्। व्यूढां द्रुपदपुत्रेण तव शिष्येण धीमता।।1.3।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: In it are heroes and great bowmen; the equals in battle of Arjuna, Bheema, Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada—all great soldiers.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: In it are heroes and great bowmen; the equals in battle of Arjuna, Bheema, Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada—all great soldiers.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अत्र शूरा महेष्वासा भीमार्जुनसमा युधि। युयुधानो विराटश्च द्रुपदश्च महारथः।।1.4।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitan, the valiant king of Benares, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya—a master of many.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitan, the valiant king of Benares, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya—a master of many.
metadata.sanskrit_text: धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान्। पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः।।1.5।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Yudhamanyu, Uttamouja, Soubhadra, and the sons of Droupadi—all famous men.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Yudhamanyu, Uttamouja, Soubhadra, and the sons of Droupadi—all famous men.
metadata.sanskrit_text: युधामन्युश्च विक्रान्त उत्तमौजाश्च वीर्यवान्। सौभद्रो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्व एव महारथाः।।1.6।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: No changes needed.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: No changes needed.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम। नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते।।1.7।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: You come first; then Bheeshma, Karna, Kripa, great warriors; Ashwaththama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadhatta;
metadata.sanskrit_text: भवान्भीष्मश्च कर्णश्च कृपश्च समितिञ्जयः। अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च सौमदत्तिस्तथैव च।।1.8।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And many others, all ready to die for My sake; all armed, all skilled in warfare.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And many others, all ready to die for My sake; all armed, all skilled in warfare.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः। नानाशस्त्रप्रहरणाः सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः।।1.9।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Yet our army seems weaker, though commanded by Bhishma; their army seems stronger, though commanded by Bhima.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Yet our army seems weaker, though commanded by Bhishma; their army seems stronger, though commanded by Bhima.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अपर्याप्तं तदस्माकं बलं भीष्माभिरक्षितम्। पर्याप्तं त्विदमेतेषां बलं भीमाभिरक्षितम्।।1.10।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Therefore, let the rank and file stand firm in their posts according to battalions, and all you generals around Bheeshma.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, let the rank and file stand firm in their posts according to battalions, and all you generals around Bheeshma.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अयनेषु च सर्वेषु यथाभागमवस्थिताः। भीष्ममेवाभिरक्षन्तु भवन्तः सर्व एव हि।।1.11।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Then, to enliven his spirits, the brave Grandfather Bheeshma, the eldest of the Kuru clan, blew his conch, its sound resembling that of a lion's roar.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Then, to enliven his spirits, the brave Grandfather Bheeshma, the eldest of the Kuru clan, blew his conch, its sound resembling that of a lion's roar.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्य संजनयन्हर्षं कुरुवृद्धः पितामहः। सिंहनादं विनद्योच्चैः शङ्खं दध्मौ प्रतापवान्।।1.12।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And immediately, all the conches, drums, trumpets, and horns blared forth in a tumultuous uproar.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And immediately, all the conches, drums, trumpets, and horns blared forth in a tumultuous uproar.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ततः शङ्खाश्च भेर्यश्च पणवानकगोमुखाः। सहसैवाभ्यहन्यन्त स शब्दस्तुमुलोऽभवत्।।1.13।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Then, seated in their spacious war chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their divine conch shells.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Then, seated in their spacious war chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their divine conch shells.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ततः श्वेतैर्हयैर्युक्ते महति स्यन्दने स्थितौ। माधवः पाण्डवश्चैव दिव्यौ शङ्खौ प्रदध्मतुः।।1.14।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya, and Arjuna blew his Devadatta; brave Bheema blew his renowned shell, Poundra.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya, and Arjuna blew his Devadatta; brave Bheema blew his renowned shell, Poundra.
metadata.sanskrit_text: पाञ्चजन्यं हृषीकेशो देवदत्तं धनंजयः। पौण्ड्रं दध्मौ महाशङ्खं भीमकर्मा वृकोदरः।।1.15।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, Nakula, and Sahadeva, the Sughosa and Manipushpaka, respectively.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, Nakula, and Sahadeva, the Sughosa and Manipushpaka, respectively.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अनन्तविजयं राजा कुन्तीपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। नकुलः सहदेवश्च सुघोषमणिपुष्पकौ।।1.16।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And the Maharaja of Benares, the great archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier, Dhrishtayumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the invincible one,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And the Maharaja of Benares, the great archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier, Dhrishtayumna, Virata, and Satyaki, the invincible one,
metadata.sanskrit_text: काश्यश्च परमेष्वासः शिखण्डी च महारथः। धृष्टद्युम्नो विराटश्च सात्यकिश्चापराजितः।।1.17।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And, O King! Drupada's sons, Droupadi's sons, and the great soldier Soubhadra blew their conches.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And, O King! Drupada's sons, Droupadi's sons, and the great soldier Soubhadra blew their conches.
metadata.sanskrit_text: द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते। सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्।।1.18।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, shaking heaven and earth with its echoing violence.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, shaking heaven and earth with its echoing violence.
metadata.sanskrit_text: स घोषो धार्तराष्ट्राणां हृदयानि व्यदारयत्। नभश्च पृथिवीं चैव तुमुलो व्यनुनादयन्।।1.19।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Then, upon beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the battlefield, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose flag bore the image of Hanuman,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Then, upon beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the battlefield, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose flag bore the image of Hanuman,
metadata.sanskrit_text: अथ व्यवस्थितान् दृष्ट्वा धार्तराष्ट्रान्कपिध्वजः। प्रवृत्ते शस्त्रसंपाते धनुरुद्यम्य पाण्डवः।।1.20।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Raising his bow, he spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible Lord of the earth! Please draw up my chariot between the two armies.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Raising his bow, he spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible Lord of the earth! Please draw up my chariot between the two armies.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच हृषीकेशं तदा वाक्यमिदमाह महीपते। सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये रथं स्थापय मेऽच्युत।।1.21।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: So that I may observe those who must fight on my side and those who must fight against me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: So that I may observe those who must fight on my side and those who must fight against me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यावदेतान्निरीक्षेऽहं योद्धुकामानवस्थितान्। कैर्मया सह योद्धव्यमस्मिन्रणसमुद्यमे।।1.22।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And gaze upon this array of soldiers, eager to please the sons of Dhritarashtra who are sinful.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And gaze upon this array of soldiers, eager to please the sons of Dhritarashtra who are sinful.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योत्स्यमानानवेक्षेऽहं य एतेऽत्र समागताः। धार्तराष्ट्रस्य दुर्बुद्धेर्युद्धे प्रियचिकीर्षवः।।1.23।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Sanjaya said: "Having listened to Arjuna's request, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His bright chariot in the midst between the two armies.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Sanjaya said: "Having listened to Arjuna's request, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His bright chariot in the midst between the two armies.
metadata.sanskrit_text: संजय उवाच एवमुक्तो हृषीकेशो गुडाकेशेन भारत। सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये स्थापयित्वा रथोत्तमम्।।1.24।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Where Bheeshma and Drona had led all the rulers of the earth, they spoke thus: O Arjuna! Behold, these members of the family of Kuru are assembled.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Where Bheeshma and Drona had led all the rulers of the earth, they spoke thus: O Arjuna! Behold, these members of the family of Kuru are assembled.
metadata.sanskrit_text: भीष्मद्रोणप्रमुखतः सर्वेषां च महीक्षिताम्। उवाच पार्थ पश्यैतान्समवेतान्कुरूनिति।।1.25।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: There, Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, and friends.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: There, Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, and friends.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्रापश्यत्स्थितान्पार्थः पितृ़नथ पितामहान्। आचार्यान्मातुलान्भ्रातृ़न्पुत्रान्पौत्रान्सखींस्तथा।।1.26।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Fathers-in-law and benefactors were arrayed on both sides, and Arjuna then gazed at all those kinsmen before him.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Fathers-in-law and benefactors were arrayed on both sides, and Arjuna then gazed at all those kinsmen before him.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्वशुरान्सुहृदश्चैव सेनयोरुभयोरपि। तान्समीक्ष्य स कौन्तेयः सर्वान्बन्धूनवस्थितान्।।1.27।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: And his heart melted with pity, and sadly he spoke: "O my Lord! When I see all these, my own people, thirsting for battle,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: And his heart melted with pity, and sadly he spoke: "O my Lord! When I see all these, my own people, thirsting for battle,
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत्। दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम्।।1.28।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: My limbs are failing me, my throat is parched, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: My limbs are failing me, my throat is parched, my body is trembling, and my hair is standing on end.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति। वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते।।1.29।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot remain still, for my mind is in tumult.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The bow Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot remain still, for my mind is in tumult.
metadata.sanskrit_text: गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते। न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः।।1.30।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The omens are unfavorable; what good can come from the slaughter of my people on this battlefield?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The omens are unfavorable; what good can come from the slaughter of my people on this battlefield?
metadata.sanskrit_text: निमित्तानि च पश्यामि विपरीतानि केशव। न च श्रेयोऽनुपश्यामि हत्वा स्वजनमाहवे।।1.31।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Ah, my Lord! I do not crave victory, nor a kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Ah, my Lord! I do not crave victory, nor a kingdom, nor any pleasure. What would a kingdom, happiness, or life be to me?
metadata.sanskrit_text: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च। किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा।।1.32।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: When those for whose sake I desire these things stand here, about to sacrifice their property and lives:

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: When those for whose sake I desire these things stand here, about to sacrifice their property and lives:
metadata.sanskrit_text: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च। त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च।।1.33।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Teachers, fathers, grandfathers, sons, grandsons, uncles, fathers-in-law, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Teachers, fathers, grandfathers, sons, grandsons, uncles, fathers-in-law, brothers-in-law, and other relatives.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आचार्याः पितरः पुत्रास्तथैव च पितामहाः। मातुलाः श्चशुराः पौत्राः श्यालाः सम्बन्धिनस्तथा।।1.34।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: I would not kill them, even for three worlds; why then for this earth alone? It matters not if I myself am killed.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: I would not kill them, even for three worlds; why then for this earth alone? It matters not if I myself am killed.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एतान्न हन्तुमिच्छामि घ्नतोऽपि मधुसूदन। अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते।।1.35।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: My Lord! What happiness can come from the death of these sons of Dhritarashtra? We shall be committing a sin if we kill these desperate men.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: My Lord! What happiness can come from the death of these sons of Dhritarashtra? We shall be committing a sin if we kill these desperate men.
metadata.sanskrit_text: निहत्य धार्तराष्ट्रान्नः का प्रीतिः स्याज्जनार्दन। पापमेवाश्रयेदस्मान्हत्वैतानाततायिनः।।1.36।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: We are worthy of a nobler feat than slaughtering our relatives—the sons of Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be happy if we kill our kinsmen?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: We are worthy of a nobler feat than slaughtering our relatives—the sons of Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be happy if we kill our kinsmen?
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्मान्नार्हा वयं हन्तुं धार्तराष्ट्रान्स्वबान्धवान्। स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव।।1.37।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Although these men, blinded by greed, see no guilt in destroying their kin or fighting against their friends,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Although these men, blinded by greed, see no guilt in destroying their kin or fighting against their friends,
metadata.sanskrit_text: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः। कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम्।।1.38।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Should we not, whose eyes are open and who consider it wrong to annihilate our family, turn away from such a great crime?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Should we not, whose eyes are open and who consider it wrong to annihilate our family, turn away from such a great crime?
metadata.sanskrit_text: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम्। कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन।।1.39।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The destruction of our kindred means the destruction of the traditions of our ancient lineage, and when these are lost, irreligion will overrun our homes.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The destruction of our kindred means the destruction of the traditions of our ancient lineage, and when these are lost, irreligion will overrun our homes.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः। धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत।।1.40।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: When irreligion spreads, the women of the house start to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the lineage follows.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: When irreligion spreads, the women of the house start to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the lineage follows.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः। स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः।।1.41।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, due to the lack of funeral cakes and ablutions.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, due to the lack of funeral cakes and ablutions.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च। पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः।।1.42।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: By the destruction of our lineage and the pollution of our blood, ancient class traditions and family purity alike perish.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: By the destruction of our lineage and the pollution of our blood, ancient class traditions and family purity alike perish.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः। उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः।।1.43।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: The wise say, my Lord, that they are forever lost whose ancient traditions have been lost.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: The wise say, my Lord, that they are forever lost whose ancient traditions have been lost.
metadata.sanskrit_text: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन। नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम।।1.44।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Alas, it is strange that we should be willing to kill our own countrymen and commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the pleasures of kingdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Alas, it is strange that we should be willing to kill our own countrymen and commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the pleasures of kingdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम्। यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः।।1.45।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: If, on the contrary, the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, should slay me, unarmed and unresisting, surely that would be better for my welfare!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: If, on the contrary, the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in hand, should slay me, unarmed and unresisting, surely that would be better for my welfare!
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः। धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत्।।1.46।।

document:
Chapter: Arjuna Visada Yoga
Meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
Translation: Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank into the seat of his chariot, discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed with grief in the midst of the armies."

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Arjuna's Dilemma
metadata.english_translation: Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, Arjuna sank into the seat of his chariot, discarding his bow and arrow, overwhelmed with grief in the midst of the armies."
metadata.sanskrit_text: सञ्जय उवाच एवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत्। विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः।।1.47।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Sanjaya then told how the Lord Shri Krishna, seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with compassion, his eyes dimmed with flowing tears and full of despondency, consoled him:

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Sanjaya then told how the Lord Shri Krishna, seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with compassion, his eyes dimmed with flowing tears and full of despondency, consoled him:
metadata.sanskrit_text: सञ्जय उवाच तं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम्। विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः।।2.1।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The Lord said: My beloved friend! Why yield to this weakness, on the eve of battle, which does no credit to those who call themselves Aryans and only brings them infamy, barring them from the gates of heaven?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The Lord said: My beloved friend! Why yield to this weakness, on the eve of battle, which does no credit to those who call themselves Aryans and only brings them infamy, barring them from the gates of heaven?
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्। अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन।।2.2।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O thou, who art the terror of thy enemies! Shake off such shameful effeminacy and make ready to act!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O thou, who art the terror of thy enemies! Shake off such shameful effeminacy and make ready to act!
metadata.sanskrit_text: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते। क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप।।2.3।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Arjuna argued: My Lord! How can I, when the battle rages, send an arrow through Bheeshma and Drona, whom I should revere?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna argued: My Lord! How can I, when the battle rages, send an arrow through Bheeshma and Drona, whom I should revere?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन। इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन।।2.4।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Rather, I would be content with a beggar's crust than to kill these teachers of mine, these precious noble souls! To slay these masters who are my benefactors would be to stain the sweetness of life's pleasures with their blood.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Rather, I would be content with a beggar's crust than to kill these teachers of mine, these precious noble souls! To slay these masters who are my benefactors would be to stain the sweetness of life's pleasures with their blood.
metadata.sanskrit_text: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान् श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके। हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैव भुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान्।।2.5।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Nor can I say whether it would be better for them to conquer me or for me to conquer them, since I would no longer care to live if I killed these sons of Dhritarashtra, who are now preparing for battle.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Nor can I say whether it would be better for them to conquer me or for me to conquer them, since I would no longer care to live if I killed these sons of Dhritarashtra, who are now preparing for battle.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयो यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः। यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषाम स्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः।।2.6।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: My heart is oppressed with pity, and my mind is confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Your disciple. Please direct me, I pray.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावः पृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः। यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मे शिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम्।।2.7।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: For even if I were to attain the monarchy of the visible world, or the sovereignty over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish that is now paralyzing my senses.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: For even if I were to attain the monarchy of the visible world, or the sovereignty over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish that is now paralyzing my senses.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्या द्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्। अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम् राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्।।2.8।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would not fight, and became silent, O King!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would not fight, and became silent, O King!
metadata.sanskrit_text: सञ्जय उवाच एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप। न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह।।2.9।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Thereupon, the Lord, with a gracious smile, addressed him who was so much depressed in the midst of the two armies.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Thereupon, the Lord, with a gracious smile, addressed him who was so much depressed in the midst of the two armies.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत। सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः।।2.10।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, yet professing wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, yet professing wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच अशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे। गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः।।2.11।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: There was never a time when I was not, nor you, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to exist.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः। न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम्।।2.12।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: As the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age in this body, so finally it passes into another; the wise have no delusion about this.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: As the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age in this body, so finally it passes into another; the wise have no delusion about this.
metadata.sanskrit_text: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा। तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति।।2.13।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Those external relations that bring cold and heat, pain and happiness come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Those external relations that bring cold and heat, pain and happiness come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!
metadata.sanskrit_text: मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः। आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत।।2.14।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstances, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, is only fit for immortality.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstances, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, is only fit for immortality.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ। समदुःखसुखं धीरं सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते।।2.15।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: That which is not shall never be; that which is shall never cease to be. These truths are self-evident to the wise.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: That which is not shall never be; that which is shall never cease to be. These truths are self-evident to the wise.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः। उभयोरपि दृष्टोऽन्तस्त्वनयोस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः।।2.16।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The Spirit, which pervades all that is seen, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy it.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The Spirit, which pervades all that is seen, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy it.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्। विनाशमव्ययस्यास्य न कश्चित् कर्तुमर्हति।।2.17।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The material bodies that this Eternal, Indestructible, and Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite; therefore, fight, O valiant man!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The material bodies that this Eternal, Indestructible, and Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite; therefore, fight, O valiant man!
metadata.sanskrit_text: अन्तवन्त इमे देहा नित्यस्योक्ताः शरीरिणः। अनाशिनोऽप्रमेयस्य तस्माद्युध्यस्व भारत।।2.18।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He who thinks that the Spirit kills, and he who thinks of it as killed, are both ignorant. The Spirit neither kills nor is it killed.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He who thinks that the Spirit kills, and he who thinks of it as killed, are both ignorant. The Spirit neither kills nor is it killed.
metadata.sanskrit_text: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम्। उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते।।2.19।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: It was not born; it will never die, nor, once having been, can it cease to exist. Unborn, eternal, ever-enduring, yet most ancient, the spirit does not die when the body is dead.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: It was not born; it will never die, nor, once having been, can it cease to exist. Unborn, eternal, ever-enduring, yet most ancient, the spirit does not die when the body is dead.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचि न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे।।2.20।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He who knows the Spirit to be indestructible, immortal, unborn, and always the same, how should he kill or cause to be killed?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He who knows the Spirit to be indestructible, immortal, unborn, and always the same, how should he kill or cause to be killed?
metadata.sanskrit_text: वेदाविनाशिनं नित्यं य एनमजमव्ययम्। कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम्।।2.21।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new ones, so the Spirit throws off its worn-out bodies and takes on fresh ones.
metadata.sanskrit_text: वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि। तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णा न्यन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही।।2.22।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Weapons cannot cleave it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot drench it, and wind cannot dry it.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Weapons cannot cleave it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot drench it, and wind cannot dry it.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः। न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।2.23।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: It is impenetrable; it cannot be drowned, scorched, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervasive, unchanging, immovable, and most ancient.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: It is impenetrable; it cannot be drowned, scorched, or dried. It is eternal, all-pervasive, unchanging, immovable, and most ancient.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अच्छेद्योऽयमदाह्योऽयमक्लेद्योऽशोष्य एव च। नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः।।2.24।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable. Therefore, knowing the Spirit as such, you have no cause to grieve.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable. Therefore, knowing the Spirit as such, you have no cause to grieve.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयमुच्यते। तस्मादेवं विदित्वैनं नानुशोचितुमर्हसि।।2.25।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Even if thou thinkest of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, O Mighty Man, thou still hast no cause to grieve.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Even if thou thinkest of it as constantly being born and constantly dying, O Mighty Man, thou still hast no cause to grieve.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम्। तथापि त्वं महाबाहो नैवं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.26।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: For death is certain for that which is born, just as birth is certain for that which is dead. Therefore, do not grieve for what is inevitable.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: For death is certain for that which is born, just as birth is certain for that which is dead. Therefore, do not grieve for what is inevitable.
metadata.sanskrit_text: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च। तस्मादपरिहार्येऽर्थे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.27।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The end and beginning of beings are unknown; we only see the intervening formations. So, what is there to grieve about?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The end and beginning of beings are unknown; we only see the intervening formations. So, what is there to grieve about?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत। अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना।।2.28।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: One hears of the Spirit with surprise, another thinks it marvelous, the third listens without comprehending. Thus, though many are told about it, scarcely is there one who knows it.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: One hears of the Spirit with surprise, another thinks it marvelous, the third listens without comprehending. Thus, though many are told about it, scarcely is there one who knows it.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेन माश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्यः। आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः श्रृणोति श्रुत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित्।।2.29।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Do not be anxious about these armies; the spirit in man is imperishable.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Do not be anxious about these armies; the spirit in man is imperishable.
metadata.sanskrit_text: देही नित्यमवध्योऽयं देहे सर्वस्य भारत। तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि।।2.30।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: You must look at your duty. Nothing can be more welcome to a soldier than a righteous war. Therefore, wavering in this resolve is unworthy, O Arjuna!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: You must look at your duty. Nothing can be more welcome to a soldier than a righteous war. Therefore, wavering in this resolve is unworthy, O Arjuna!
metadata.sanskrit_text: स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि। धर्म्याद्धि युद्धाछ्रेयोऽन्यत्क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यते।।2.31।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Blessed are the soldiers who find their opportunity; this opportunity has opened for thee the gates of heaven.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Blessed are the soldiers who find their opportunity; this opportunity has opened for thee the gates of heaven.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदृच्छया चोपपन्नं स्वर्गद्वारमपावृतम्। सुखिनः क्षत्रियाः पार्थ लभन्ते युद्धमीदृशम्।।2.32।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Refuse to fight in this righteous cause, and you will be a traitor, losing fame, incurring only sin.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Refuse to fight in this righteous cause, and you will be a traitor, losing fame, incurring only sin.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अथ चैत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि। ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.33।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Men will talk forever of thy disgrace; and to the noble, dishonor is worse than death.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Men will talk forever of thy disgrace; and to the noble, dishonor is worse than death.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्। संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते।।2.34।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Great generals will think that you have fled from the battlefield out of cowardice; though once honored, you will seem despicable.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Great generals will think that you have fled from the battlefield out of cowardice; though once honored, you will seem despicable.
metadata.sanskrit_text: भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः। येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्।।2.35।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Your enemies will spread scandal and mock your courage. Is there anything more humiliating?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Your enemies will spread scandal and mock your courage. Is there anything more humiliating?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः। निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।2.36।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: If you are killed, you will attain Heaven; if you are victorious, you will enjoy the kingdom of earth. Therefore, arise, O Son of Kunti, and fight!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: If you are killed, you will attain Heaven; if you are victorious, you will enjoy the kingdom of earth. Therefore, arise, O Son of Kunti, and fight!
metadata.sanskrit_text: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्। तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।2.37।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye. Be prepared for the combat, and you will commit no sin.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye. Be prepared for the combat, and you will commit no sin.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ। ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.38।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: I have told you the philosophy of knowledge. Now, listen, and I will explain the philosophy of action, by means of which, O Arjuna, you will break through the bondage of all action.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: I have told you the philosophy of knowledge. Now, listen, and I will explain the philosophy of action, by means of which, O Arjuna, you will break through the bondage of all action.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु। बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि।।2.39।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: On this path, endeavour is never wasted nor repressed. Even a little practice of it protects one from great danger.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: On this path, endeavour is never wasted nor repressed. Even a little practice of it protects one from great danger.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते। स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।2.40।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: By its means, the straying intellect becomes steadied in contemplating one object only; whereas the minds of the irresolute stray into innumerable bypaths.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: By its means, the straying intellect becomes steadied in contemplating one object only; whereas the minds of the irresolute stray into innumerable bypaths.
metadata.sanskrit_text: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन। बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्।।2.41।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Only the ignorant speak in figurative language; it is they who extol the letter of the scriptures, saying, "There is nothing deeper than this."

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Only the ignorant speak in figurative language; it is they who extol the letter of the scriptures, saying, "There is nothing deeper than this."
metadata.sanskrit_text: यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः। वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः।।2.42।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Consulting only their own desires, they construct their own heaven, devising arduous and complex rites to secure their own pleasure and power; and the only result is rebirth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Consulting only their own desires, they construct their own heaven, devising arduous and complex rites to secure their own pleasure and power; and the only result is rebirth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्। क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।2.43।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: While their minds are absorbed with thoughts of power and personal enjoyment, they cannot focus their discrimination on one point.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: While their minds are absorbed with thoughts of power and personal enjoyment, they cannot focus their discrimination on one point.
metadata.sanskrit_text: भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्। व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।2.44।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The Vedic Scriptures tell of the three constituents of life—the Qualities. Rise above all of them, O Arjuna, above all the pairs of opposing sensations; be steadfast in truth, free from worldly anxieties, and centered in the Self.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The Vedic Scriptures tell of the three constituents of life—the Qualities. Rise above all of them, O Arjuna, above all the pairs of opposing sensations; be steadfast in truth, free from worldly anxieties, and centered in the Self.
metadata.sanskrit_text: त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन। निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.45।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can extract from any scripture that which will serve their purpose.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can extract from any scripture that which will serve their purpose.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके। तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।2.46।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: But you have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: But you have only the right to work, but none to the fruit of it. Let not the fruit of your action be your motive; nor be you enamored of inaction.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि।।2.47।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Revised: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Revised: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय। सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते।।2.48।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine. Therefore, have recourse to Pure Intelligence. It is only the small-minded who work for reward.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine. Therefore, have recourse to Pure Intelligence. It is only the small-minded who work for reward.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय। बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः।।2.49।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: When a person attains Pure Reason, they renounce in this world the results of both good and evil. Cling to Right Action. Spirituality is the true art of living.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: When a person attains Pure Reason, they renounce in this world the results of both good and evil. Cling to Right Action. Spirituality is the true art of living.
metadata.sanskrit_text: बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते। तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।2.50।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The sages, guided by pure intellect, renounce the fruits of their actions; and, thus freed from the shackles of rebirth, they attain the highest bliss.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The sages, guided by pure intellect, renounce the fruits of their actions; and, thus freed from the shackles of rebirth, they attain the highest bliss.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः। जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्।।2.51।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: When your reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then you will become indifferent to both the philosophies you have heard and those you may yet hear.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: When your reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then you will become indifferent to both the philosophies you have heard and those you may yet hear.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति। तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च।।2.52।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scriptures, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the infinite, then you have attained spirituality.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scriptures, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the infinite, then you have attained spirituality.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला। समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।2.53।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognize the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? How does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognize the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? How does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव। स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्।।2.54।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: When a person has given up the desires of their heart and is content with the Self alone, they have surely reached the highest state.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: When a person has given up the desires of their heart and is content with the Self alone, they have surely reached the highest state.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्। आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते।।2.55।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The sage whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not aroused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger, or fear—take him to be one who stands at a lofty level.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The sage whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not aroused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger, or fear—take him to be one who stands at a lofty level.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः। वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते।।2.56।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He who, wherever he goes, is not attached to any person or place by ties of flesh; who accepts good and evil alike, neither welcoming the one nor shrinking from the other—take him to be one who is merged in the Infinite.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He who, wherever he goes, is not attached to any person or place by ties of flesh; who accepts good and evil alike, neither welcoming the one nor shrinking from the other—take him to be one who is merged in the Infinite.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्। नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.57।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within its shell—take it that such a one has attained perfection.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within its shell—take it that such a one has attained perfection.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.58।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The objects of sense turn away from him who is abstinent. Even the taste for them is lost in him who has seen the Truth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The objects of sense turn away from him who is abstinent. Even the taste for them is lost in him who has seen the Truth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः। रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते।।2.59।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: O Arjuna! The mind of one who is attempting to conquer it is forcibly carried away, in spite of their efforts, by their tumultuous senses.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: O Arjuna! The mind of one who is attempting to conquer it is forcibly carried away, in spite of their efforts, by their tumultuous senses.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः। इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः।।2.60।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Restraining them all, let him steadfastly meditate on Me; for whoever conquers their senses achieves perfection.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Restraining them all, let him steadfastly meditate on Me; for whoever conquers their senses achieves perfection.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः। वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.61।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: When a person dwells on the objects of sense, they create an attraction for them; this attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: When a person dwells on the objects of sense, they create an attraction for them; this attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते। सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।2.62।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Anger induces delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory results in the shattering of reason; and the destruction of reason leads to destruction.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Anger induces delusion; delusion leads to loss of memory; loss of memory results in the shattering of reason; and the destruction of reason leads to destruction.
metadata.sanskrit_text: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः। स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति।।2.63।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: But the self-controlled soul, who moves among sense objects, free from attachment or repulsion, wins eternal peace.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: But the self-controlled soul, who moves among sense objects, free from attachment or repulsion, wins eternal peace.
metadata.sanskrit_text: रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्। आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति।।2.64।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Having attained peace, he becomes free from misery; for when the mind gains peace, right discrimination follows.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Having attained peace, he becomes free from misery; for when the mind gains peace, right discrimination follows.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते। प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Right discrimination is not for him who cannot concentrate. Without concentration, there cannot be meditation; he who cannot meditate must not expect peace; and without peace, how can one expect happiness?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Right discrimination is not for him who cannot concentrate. Without concentration, there cannot be meditation; he who cannot meditate must not expect peace; and without peace, how can one expect happiness?
metadata.sanskrit_text: नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना। न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्।।2.66।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते। तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: Therefore, O Mighty-Armed One, he whose senses are detached from their objects—take it that his reason is purified.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, O Mighty-Armed One, he whose senses are detached from their objects—take it that his reason is purified.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: The saint is awake when the world sleeps, and he disregards that for which the world lives.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: The saint is awake when the world sleeps, and he disregards that for which the world lives.
metadata.sanskrit_text: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी। यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He attains peace into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which, though brimming with water, remains ever the same; not he whom desires carry away.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He attains peace into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which, though brimming with water, remains ever the same; not he whom desires carry away.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्। तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: He attains peace who, giving up desire, moves through the world without aspiration, possessing nothing that he can call his own and is free from pride.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: He attains peace who, giving up desire, moves through the world without aspiration, possessing nothing that he can call his own and is free from pride.
metadata.sanskrit_text: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः। निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।

document:
Chapter: Sankhya Yoga
Meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
Translation: O Arjuna! This is the state of the Self, the Supreme Spirit, to which, if one attains, it shall never be taken away. Even at the time of leaving the body, one will remain firmly enthroned there and become one with the Eternal.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Transcendental Knowledge
metadata.english_translation: O Arjuna! This is the state of the Self, the Supreme Spirit, to which, if one attains, it shall never be taken away. Even at the time of leaving the body, one will remain firmly enthroned there and become one with the Eternal.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति। स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Arjuna questioned: My Lord! If wisdom is superior to action, why do you advise me to engage in this terrible fight?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna questioned: My Lord! If wisdom is superior to action, why do you advise me to engage in this terrible fight?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन। तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Your language confuses me and confounds my reason. Therefore, please tell me the only way by which I can, without doubt, secure my spiritual welfare.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Your language confuses me and confounds my reason. Therefore, please tell me the only way by which I can, without doubt, secure my spiritual welfare.
metadata.sanskrit_text: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे। तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम्।।3.2।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: In this world, as I have said, there is a twofold path, O sinless one! There is the path of wisdom for those who meditate, and the path of action for those who work.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: In this world, as I have said, there is a twofold path, O sinless one! There is the path of wisdom for those who meditate, and the path of action for those who work.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ। ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्।।3.3।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: No one can attain freedom from action by abstaining from action, nor can they reach perfection by simply not acting.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: No one can attain freedom from action by abstaining from action, nor can they reach perfection by simply not acting.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते। न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति।।3.4।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: He cannot remain inactive even for a moment, for the qualities of Nature will compel him to act, whether he wills it or not.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: He cannot remain inactive even for a moment, for the qualities of Nature will compel him to act, whether he wills it or not.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न हि कश्िचत्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत्। कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः।।3.5।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: He who remains motionless, refusing to act, yet brooding over sensuous objects, is that deluded soul simply a hypocrite.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: He who remains motionless, refusing to act, yet brooding over sensuous objects, is that deluded soul simply a hypocrite.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्। इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते।।3.6।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: But, O Arjuna! All honor to him whose mind controls his senses, for he is thereby beginning to practice Karma-Yoga, the Path of Right Action, keeping himself always unattached.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: But, O Arjuna! All honor to him whose mind controls his senses, for he is thereby beginning to practice Karma-Yoga, the Path of Right Action, keeping himself always unattached.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन। कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते।।3.7।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Do your duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if one remained inactive.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Do your duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if one remained inactive.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः। शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।3.8।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: In this world, people are fettered by their actions, unless they are performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let your actions be done without attachment, as a sacrifice only.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: In this world, people are fettered by their actions, unless they are performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let your actions be done without attachment, as a sacrifice only.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः। तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।3.9।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: In the beginning, when God created all beings through the sacrifice of Himself, He said to them: "You can procreate through sacrifice, and it shall satisfy all your desires."

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: In the beginning, when God created all beings through the sacrifice of Himself, He said to them: "You can procreate through sacrifice, and it shall satisfy all your desires."
metadata.sanskrit_text: सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः। अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक्।।3.10।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Worship the powers of Nature, and let them nourish you in return; thus, supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Worship the powers of Nature, and let them nourish you in return; thus, supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.
metadata.sanskrit_text: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः। परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ।।3.11।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: For, fed by sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a thief.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: For, fed by sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a thief.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः। तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः।।3.12।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: The sages who enjoy the food that remains after the sacrifice is made are freed from all sins; whereas, the selfish who spread their feast only for themselves feed on sin alone.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: The sages who enjoy the food that remains after the sacrifice is made are freed from all sins; whereas, the selfish who spread their feast only for themselves feed on sin alone.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः। भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात्।।3.13।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: All creatures are the product of food; food is the product of rain; rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is the noblest form of action.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: All creatures are the product of food; food is the product of rain; rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is the noblest form of action.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः। यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः।।3.14।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: All actions originate from the Supreme Spirit, which is Imperishable, and in sacrificial actions, the all-pervasive Spirit is consciously present.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: All actions originate from the Supreme Spirit, which is Imperishable, and in sacrificial actions, the all-pervasive Spirit is consciously present.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम्। तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम्।।3.15।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Thus, he who does not help the revolving wheel of sacrifice, but instead leads a sinful life, rejoicing in the gratification of his senses, O Arjuna, is breathing in vain.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Thus, he who does not help the revolving wheel of sacrifice, but instead leads a sinful life, rejoicing in the gratification of his senses, O Arjuna, is breathing in vain.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः। अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति।।3.16।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: On the other hand, the soul who meditates on the Self is content to serve the Self and rests satisfied in the Self; there is nothing more for them to accomplish.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: On the other hand, the soul who meditates on the Self is content to serve the Self and rests satisfied in the Self; there is nothing more for them to accomplish.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः। आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते।।3.17।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: He has nothing to gain from the performance or non-performance of action; his welfare does not depend on any contribution that an earthly creature can make.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: He has nothing to gain from the performance or non-performance of action; his welfare does not depend on any contribution that an earthly creature can make.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन। न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्िचदर्थव्यपाश्रयः।।3.18।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Therefore, do your duty perfectly, without worrying about the results, for he who does his duty without attachment attains the Supreme.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, do your duty perfectly, without worrying about the results, for he who does his duty without attachment attains the Supreme.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर। असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः।।3.19।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of enlightening the world, it is your duty to act.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of enlightening the world, it is your duty to act.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः। लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि।।3.20।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: For whatever a great man does, others imitate; people conform to the standard he has set.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: For whatever a great man does, others imitate; people conform to the standard he has set.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः। स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते।।3.21।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: There is nothing in this universe, O Arjuna, that I am compelled to do, nor anything for me to attain; yet I persistently remain active.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: There is nothing in this universe, O Arjuna, that I am compelled to do, nor anything for me to attain; yet I persistently remain active.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन। नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि।।3.22।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Were I not to act without ceasing, O prince, people would be inclined to do the same.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Were I not to act without ceasing, O prince, people would be inclined to do the same.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः। मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।3.23।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: And if I were to refrain from action, the human race would be ruined; I would lead the world to chaos, and destruction would follow.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: And if I were to refrain from action, the human race would be ruined; I would lead the world to chaos, and destruction would follow.
metadata.sanskrit_text: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्। सङ्करस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः।।3.24।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: As the ignorant act, out of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: As the ignorant act, out of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत। कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्िचकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्।।3.25।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
