Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: But a wise man should not disturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all others to do the same.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: But a wise man should not disturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all others to do the same.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम्। जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान् युक्तः समाचरन्।।3.26।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Action is the product of the qualities inherent in nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says, "I am the doer."

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Action is the product of the qualities inherent in nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says, "I am the doer."
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः। अहङ्कारविमूढात्मा कर्ताऽहमिति मन्यते।।3.27।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: But he, O Mighty One, who correctly understands the relationship between the Qualities and action, is not attached to the act, for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: But he, O Mighty One, who correctly understands the relationship between the Qualities and action, is not attached to the act, for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः। गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते।।3.28।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Those who do not understand the qualities are interested in the act; however, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of those who do not.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Those who do not understand the qualities are interested in the act; however, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of those who do not.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रकृतेर्गुणसम्मूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु। तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत्।।3.29।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Therefore, surrender your actions to Me, keep your thoughts focused on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without expecting a reward, with a mind free from excitement, begin to fight.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, surrender your actions to Me, keep your thoughts focused on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without expecting a reward, with a mind free from excitement, begin to fight.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा। निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः।।3.30।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firmly in faith and without caviling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firmly in faith and without caviling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः। श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः।।3.31।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: But they who ridicule My word and do not observe it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom, and blind. They seek only their own destruction.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: But they who ridicule My word and do not observe it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom, and blind. They seek only their own destruction.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम्। सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः।।3.32।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Even the wise man acts in accordance with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Even the wise man acts in accordance with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?
metadata.sanskrit_text: सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि। प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति।।3.33।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: The love and hate that are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them, as they only obstruct the path.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: The love and hate that are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them, as they only obstruct the path.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ। तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ।।3.34।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: It is better to do one's own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for doing the duty of another is fraught with danger.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: It is better to do one's own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for doing the duty of another is fraught with danger.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्। स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः।।3.35।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is it that drives a person to sin, even against their will and as if by compulsion?"

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is it that drives a person to sin, even against their will and as if by compulsion?"
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः। अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः।।3.36।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts all things. It is the greatest enemy of man.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts all things. It is the greatest enemy of man.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः। महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम्।।3.37।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: As fire is shrouded by smoke, a mirror is covered by dust, and a child is enveloped by the womb, so is the universe enveloped in desire.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: As fire is shrouded by smoke, a mirror is covered by dust, and a child is enveloped by the womb, so is the universe enveloped in desire.
metadata.sanskrit_text: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च। यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम्।।3.38।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: It is the wise man's constant enemy; it tarnishes the face of wisdom, being as insatiable as a flame of fire.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: It is the wise man's constant enemy; it tarnishes the face of wisdom, being as insatiable as a flame of fire.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा। कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च।।3.39।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: It works through the senses, the mind, and the reason; and with their help, it destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: It works through the senses, the mind, and the reason; and with their help, it destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते। एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम्।।3.40।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, first control your senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin and is the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, O Arjuna, first control your senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin and is the destroyer of knowledge and wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ। पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम्।।3.41।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: It is said that the senses are powerful; however, beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and greater than the intellect is He.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: It is said that the senses are powerful; however, beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and greater than the intellect is He.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः। मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः।।3.42।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Yoga
Meaning: Path of Selfless Service
Translation: Thus, O Mighty-Armed One, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect, and with His help, subdue your personal ego and kill your enemy, Desire, even though it is extremely difficult.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Selfless Service
metadata.english_translation: Thus, O Mighty-Armed One, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect, and with His help, subdue your personal ego and kill your enemy, Desire, even though it is extremely difficult.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना। जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम्।।3.43।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: I taught this imperishable philosophy to Vivaswān, the founder of the Sun dynasty; Vivaswān gave it to Manu, the lawgiver, and Manu to King Ikshvāku.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: I taught this imperishable philosophy to Vivaswān, the founder of the Sun dynasty; Vivaswān gave it to Manu, the lawgiver, and Manu to King Ikshvāku.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम्। विवस्वान् मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत्।।4.1।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: The Divine Kings knew it, for it was their tradition; then, after a long time, it was at last forgotten.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: The Divine Kings knew it, for it was their tradition; then, after a long time, it was at last forgotten.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः। स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप।।4.2।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: It is the same ancient path that I have now revealed to you, for you are my devotee and my friend. It is the supreme secret.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: It is the same ancient path that I have now revealed to you, for you are my devotee and my friend. It is the supreme secret.
metadata.sanskrit_text: स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः। भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम्।।4.3।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Arjuna asked: My Lord! Vyasawana was born before You; how then can You have revealed it to him?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked: My Lord! Vyasawana was born before You; how then can You have revealed it to him?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः। कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति।।4.4।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to me, but yours are unknown to you.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too, O Arjuna! My births are known to me, but yours are unknown to you.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन। तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप।।4.5।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: There is no beginning to Me. Though I am imperishable and the Lord of all that exists, I manifest Myself by My own will and power.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: There is no beginning to Me. Though I am imperishable and the Lord of all that exists, I manifest Myself by My own will and power.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन्। प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया।।4.6।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Whenever spirituality decays and materialism is rampant, then, O Arjuna, I reincarnate myself.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Whenever spirituality decays and materialism is rampant, then, O Arjuna, I reincarnate myself.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदाऽऽत्मानं सृजाम्यहम्।।4.7।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked, and to establish the kingdom of God, I am reborn from age to age.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked, and to establish the kingdom of God, I am reborn from age to age.
metadata.sanskrit_text: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे।।4.8।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: He who realizes the divine truth concerning My birth and life does not take birth again; and when he leaves his body, he becomes one with Me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: He who realizes the divine truth concerning My birth and life does not take birth again; and when he leaves his body, he becomes one with Me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः। त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन।।4.9।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Many have merged their existences in Mine, being freed from desire, fear, and anger, always filled with Me and purified by the illuminating flame of self-abnegation.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Many have merged their existences in Mine, being freed from desire, fear, and anger, always filled with Me and purified by the illuminating flame of self-abnegation.
metadata.sanskrit_text: वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः। बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः।।4.10।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: However men try to worship Me, I welcome them. Whatever path they take, it leads to Me in the end.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: However men try to worship Me, I welcome them. Whatever path they take, it leads to Me in the end.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम्। मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः।।4.11।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Those who seek success worship the Powers, and their actions in this world bear immediate fruit.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Those who seek success worship the Powers, and their actions in this world bear immediate fruit.
metadata.sanskrit_text: काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः। क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा।।4.12।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: The four divisions of society—the wise, the soldier, the merchant, and the laborer—were created by Me, according to the natural distribution of qualities and instincts. I am the author of them, though I Myself do not act and am changeless.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: The four divisions of society—the wise, the soldier, the merchant, and the laborer—were created by Me, according to the natural distribution of qualities and instincts. I am the author of them, though I Myself do not act and am changeless.
metadata.sanskrit_text: चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः। तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम्।।4.13।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: My actions do not bind Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring. He who thus realizes Me is not enslaved by action.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: My actions do not bind Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring. He who thus realizes Me is not enslaved by action.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा। इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते।।4.14।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: In the light of wisdom, our ancestors who sought deliverance performed their acts. Act thou also as our fathers of old did.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: In the light of wisdom, our ancestors who sought deliverance performed their acts. Act thou also as our fathers of old did.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः। कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम्।।4.15।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: What is action and what is inaction? This is a question that has bewildered the wise. But I will declare to you the philosophy of action, and knowing it, you will be free from evil.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: What is action and what is inaction? This is a question that has bewildered the wise. But I will declare to you the philosophy of action, and knowing it, you will be free from evil.
metadata.sanskrit_text: किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः। तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात्।।4.16।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: It is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, for the law of action is mysterious.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: It is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, for the law of action is mysterious.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः। अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः।।4.17।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: He who can see inaction in action, and action in inaction, is the wisest among men. He is a saint, even though he still acts.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: He who can see inaction in action, and action in inaction, is the wisest among men. He is a saint, even though he still acts.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः। स बुद्धिमान् मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत्।।4.18।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: The wise call him a sage, for whatever he undertakes is free from the motive of desire, and his deeds are purified by the fire of wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: The wise call him a sage, for whatever he undertakes is free from the motive of desire, and his deeds are purified by the fire of wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः। ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः।।4.19।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, he is always contented and independent; in reality, he does nothing, even though he appears to be acting.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, he is always contented and independent; in reality, he does nothing, even though he appears to be acting.
metadata.sanskrit_text: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः। कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः।।4.20।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Expecting nothing, his mind and personality controlled, without greed, doing only bodily actions; though he acts, he remains untainted.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Expecting nothing, his mind and personality controlled, without greed, doing only bodily actions; though he acts, he remains untainted.
metadata.sanskrit_text: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः। शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्।।4.21।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Content with what comes to him without any effort of his own, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, his mind balanced in both success and failure; though he acts, the consequences do not bind him.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Content with what comes to him without any effort of his own, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, his mind balanced in both success and failure; though he acts, the consequences do not bind him.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः। समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते।।4.22।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: He who is without attachment, free, his mind centered in wisdom, and his actions done as a sacrifice, leave no trace behind.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: He who is without attachment, free, his mind centered in wisdom, and his actions done as a sacrifice, leave no trace behind.
metadata.sanskrit_text: गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः। यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते।।4.23।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: For him, the sacrifice is the Spirit; the Spirit and the offering are one; it is the Spirit that is sacrificed in its own fire, and the man, even in action, is united with God, since his mind never ceases to be fixed on Him while performing the act.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: For him, the sacrifice is the Spirit; the Spirit and the offering are one; it is the Spirit that is sacrificed in its own fire, and the man, even in action, is united with God, since his mind never ceases to be fixed on Him while performing the act.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्महविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्। ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना।।4.24।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Some sages sacrifice to the powers, while others offer themselves on the altar of the eternal.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Some sages sacrifice to the powers, while others offer themselves on the altar of the eternal.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते। ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति।।4.25।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Some sacrifice their physical senses in the fire of self-control; others offer up their contact with external objects in the sacrificial fire of their senses.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Some sacrifice their physical senses in the fire of self-control; others offer up their contact with external objects in the sacrificial fire of their senses.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति। शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति।।4.26।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Others again sacrifice their activities and vitality in the spiritual fire of self-abnegation, kindled by wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Others again sacrifice their activities and vitality in the spiritual fire of self-abnegation, kindled by wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे। आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते।।4.27।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Others offer as their sacrifice wealth, austerities, and meditation. Monks, wedded to their vows, renounce their scriptural learning and even their spiritual powers.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Others offer as their sacrifice wealth, austerities, and meditation. Monks, wedded to their vows, renounce their scriptural learning and even their spiritual powers.
metadata.sanskrit_text: द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे। स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः।।4.28।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: There are some who practice controlling the vital energy and governing the subtle forces of prana and apana, thereby sacrificing their prana to apana, or their apana to prana.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: There are some who practice controlling the vital energy and governing the subtle forces of prana and apana, thereby sacrificing their prana to apana, or their apana to prana.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अपाने जुह्वति प्राण प्राणेऽपानं तथाऽपरे। प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः।।4.29।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Others, controlling their diet, sacrifice their worldly life to the spiritual fire. All understand the principle of sacrifice, and by it their sins are washed away.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Others, controlling their diet, sacrifice their worldly life to the spiritual fire. All understand the principle of sacrifice, and by it their sins are washed away.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति। सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः।।4.30।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Tasting the nectar of immortality, as the reward of sacrifice, they reach the Eternal. This world is not for those who refuse to sacrifice; nor is the other world.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Tasting the nectar of immortality, as the reward of sacrifice, they reach the Eternal. This world is not for those who refuse to sacrifice; nor is the other world.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम्। नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतो़ऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम।।4.31।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: In this way, other sacrifices may also be undertaken for the sake of the Spirit. Know that they all depend on action. Knowing this, you will be free.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: In this way, other sacrifices may also be undertaken for the sake of the Spirit. Know that they all depend on action. Knowing this, you will be free.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे। कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे।।4.32।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: The sacrifice of wisdom is superior to any material sacrifice, for, O Arjuna, the pinnacle of action is always realization.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: The sacrifice of wisdom is superior to any material sacrifice, for, O Arjuna, the pinnacle of action is always realization.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप। सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते।।4.33।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: This you shall learn by prostrating yourself at the master's feet, questioning them, and serving them. The wise who have realized the truth will teach you wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: This you shall learn by prostrating yourself at the master's feet, questioning them, and serving them. The wise who have realized the truth will teach you wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया। उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः।।4.34।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Having known That, you shall never again be confounded; and, O Arjuna, by the power of that wisdom, you shall see all these people as if they were your own Self, and therefore as Me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Having known That, you shall never again be confounded; and, O Arjuna, by the power of that wisdom, you shall see all these people as if they were your own Self, and therefore as Me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव। येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि।।4.35।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Even if you are the greatest of sinners, you will cross over all sin by the ferryboat of wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Even if you are the greatest of sinners, you will cross over all sin by the ferryboat of wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः। सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि।।4.36।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: As the kindled fire consumes the fuel, so, O Arjuna, the embers of action are burnt to ashes in the flame of wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: As the kindled fire consumes the fuel, so, O Arjuna, the embers of action are burnt to ashes in the flame of wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन। ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा।।4.37।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: There is nothing in the world so purifying as wisdom; and he who is a perfect saint finds that at last within himself.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: There is nothing in the world so purifying as wisdom; and he who is a perfect saint finds that at last within himself.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते। तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति।।4.38।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: He who is full of faith attains wisdom, and he who can control his senses, having attained that wisdom, will soon attain Supreme Peace.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: He who is full of faith attains wisdom, and he who can control his senses, having attained that wisdom, will soon attain Supreme Peace.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः। ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।4.39।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: But the ignorant man, and he who has no faith, and the skeptic are lost. Neither in this world nor elsewhere is there any happiness in store for him who always doubts.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: But the ignorant man, and he who has no faith, and the skeptic are lost. Neither in this world nor elsewhere is there any happiness in store for him who always doubts.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति। नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः।।4.40।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: But the one who has renounced their actions for meditation, who has cleaved their doubts in two by the sword of wisdom, and who remains always enthroned in their Self, is not bound by their actions.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: But the one who has renounced their actions for meditation, who has cleaved their doubts in two by the sword of wisdom, and who remains always enthroned in their Self, is not bound by their actions.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम्। आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय।।4.41।।

document:
Chapter: Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
Translation: Therefore, cleave asunder with the sword of wisdom the doubts of the heart, which your own ignorance has engendered, and follow the path of wisdom and arise!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, cleave asunder with the sword of wisdom the doubts of the heart, which your own ignorance has engendered, and follow the path of wisdom and arise!
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्मादज्ञानसंभूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनाऽऽत्मनः। छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत।।4.42।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Arjuna said: My Lord! At one moment, You praise renunciation of action; at another, You praise right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is more conducive to my highest welfare?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna said: My Lord! At one moment, You praise renunciation of action; at another, You praise right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is more conducive to my highest welfare?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच संन्यासं कर्मणां कृष्ण पुनर्योगं च शंससि। यच्छ्रेय एतयोरेकं तन्मे ब्रूहि सुनिश्िचतम्।।5.1।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Both renunciation of action and the path of right action lead to the highest; however, right action is the better of the two.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Both renunciation of action and the path of right action lead to the highest; however, right action is the better of the two.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच संन्यासः कर्मयोगश्च निःश्रेयसकरावुभौ। तयोस्तु कर्मसंन्यासात्कर्मयोगो विशिष्यते।।5.2।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He is a true ascetic who never desires nor dislikes, who is unaffected by the opposites and is easily freed from bondage.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He is a true ascetic who never desires nor dislikes, who is unaffected by the opposites and is easily freed from bondage.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ज्ञेयः स नित्यसंन्यासी यो न द्वेष्टि न काङ्क्षति। निर्द्वन्द्वो हि महाबाहो सुखं बन्धात्प्रमुच्यते।।5.3।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Only the unenlightened speak of wisdom and right action as separate; the wise do not. If anyone knows one, they enjoy the fruit of both.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Only the unenlightened speak of wisdom and right action as separate; the wise do not. If anyone knows one, they enjoy the fruit of both.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सांख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः। एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम्।।5.4।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: The level which is attained through wisdom is also reached through right action. He who perceives that the two are one, knows the truth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: The level which is attained through wisdom is also reached through right action. He who perceives that the two are one, knows the truth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्सांख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते। एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति।।5.5।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Without concentration, O Mighty One, renunciation is difficult. But the sage who is always meditating on the Divine, shall soon attain the Absolute.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Without concentration, O Mighty One, renunciation is difficult. But the sage who is always meditating on the Divine, shall soon attain the Absolute.
metadata.sanskrit_text: संन्यासस्तु महाबाहो दुःखमाप्तुमयोगतः। योगयुक्तो मुनिर्ब्रह्म नचिरेणाधिगच्छति।।5.6।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He who is spiritual, pure, has overcome his senses and his personal self, and has realized his highest Self as the Self of all—even though he acts, he is not bound by his actions.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He who is spiritual, pure, has overcome his senses and his personal self, and has realized his highest Self as the Self of all—even though he acts, he is not bound by his actions.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योगयुक्तो विशुद्धात्मा विजितात्मा जितेन्द्रियः। सर्वभूतात्मभूतात्मा कुर्वन्नपि न लिप्यते।।5.7।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Though the saint sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps, and breathes, yet he knows the truth and knows that it is not he who acts.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Though the saint sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps, and breathes, yet he knows the truth and knows that it is not he who acts.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नैव किंचित्करोमीति युक्तो मन्येत तत्त्ववित्। पश्यन् श्रृणवन्स्पृशञ्जिघ्रन्नश्नन्गच्छन्स्वपन् श्वसन्।।5.8।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Though he talks, gives, receives, opens his eyes, and shuts them, he still knows that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Though he talks, gives, receives, opens his eyes, and shuts them, he still knows that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रलपन्विसृजन्गृह्णन्नुन्मिषन्निमिषन्नपि। इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तन्त इति धारयन्।।5.9।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः। लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा।।5.10।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: The sage performs his action dispassionately, using his body, mind, intellect, and even his senses, always as a means for purification.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: The sage performs his action dispassionately, using his body, mind, intellect, and even his senses, always as a means for purification.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कायेन मनसा बुद्ध्या केवलैरिन्द्रियैरपि। योगिनः कर्म कुर्वन्ति सङ्गं त्यक्त्वाऽऽत्मशुद्धये।।5.11।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Having abandoned the fruit of action, he wins eternal peace. Others, unacquainted with spirituality, led by desire and clinging to the benefit they think will follow their actions, become entangled in them.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Having abandoned the fruit of action, he wins eternal peace. Others, unacquainted with spirituality, led by desire and clinging to the benefit they think will follow their actions, become entangled in them.
metadata.sanskrit_text: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम्। अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते।।5.12।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled soul enjoys bliss in this body, the city of the nine gates, neither doing anything themselves nor causing anything to be done.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled soul enjoys bliss in this body, the city of the nine gates, neither doing anything themselves nor causing anything to be done.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वकर्माणि मनसा संन्यस्यास्ते सुखं वशी। नवद्वारे पुरे देही नैव कुर्वन्न कारयन्।।5.13।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: The Lord of this universe has not ordained activity, nor any incentive thereto, nor any relation between an act and its consequences; all this is the work of Nature.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: The Lord of this universe has not ordained activity, nor any incentive thereto, nor any relation between an act and its consequences; all this is the work of Nature.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न कर्तृत्वं न कर्माणि लोकस्य सृजति प्रभुः। न कर्मफलसंयोगं स्वभावस्तु प्रवर्तते।।5.14।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: The Lord does not accept responsibility for any person's sin or merit; they are deluded, for wisdom is submerged in ignorance within them.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: The Lord does not accept responsibility for any person's sin or merit; they are deluded, for wisdom is submerged in ignorance within them.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नादत्ते कस्यचित्पापं न चैव सुकृतं विभुः। अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः।।5.15।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Surely, wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth to those whose ignorance has been dispelled by the wisdom of the Self.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Surely, wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth to those whose ignorance has been dispelled by the wisdom of the Self.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ज्ञानेन तु तदज्ञानं येषां नाशितमात्मनः। तेषामादित्यवज्ज्ञानं प्रकाशयति तत्परम्।।5.16।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Meditating on the divine, having faith in the divine, concentrating on the divine, and losing themselves in the divine, their sins dissolve in wisdom, and they go from whence there is no return.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Meditating on the divine, having faith in the divine, concentrating on the divine, and losing themselves in the divine, their sins dissolve in wisdom, and they go from whence there is no return.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तद्बुद्धयस्तदात्मानस्तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः। गच्छन्त्यपुनरावृत्तिं ज्ञाननिर्धूतकल्मषाः।।5.17।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Sages look upon all equally, whether they be a minister of learning and humility, an infidel, a cow, an elephant, or a dog.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Sages look upon all equally, whether they be a minister of learning and humility, an infidel, a cow, an elephant, or a dog.
metadata.sanskrit_text: विद्याविनयसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि। शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः।।5.18।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Even in this world, those whose minds remain always balanced, fixed on the Supreme, conquer their earthly life; for the Supreme has neither blemish nor bias.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Even in this world, those whose minds remain always balanced, fixed on the Supreme, conquer their earthly life; for the Supreme has neither blemish nor bias.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः। निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः।।5.19।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He who knows and lives in the Absolute remains unmoved and unperturbed; he is not elated by pleasure nor depressed by pain.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He who knows and lives in the Absolute remains unmoved and unperturbed; he is not elated by pleasure nor depressed by pain.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम्। स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः।।5.20।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He finds happiness in his own Self and enjoys eternal bliss, whose heart does not yearn for the contacts of the earth and whose Self is one with the Everlasting.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He finds happiness in his own Self and enjoys eternal bliss, whose heart does not yearn for the contacts of the earth and whose Self is one with the Everlasting.
metadata.sanskrit_text: बाह्यस्पर्शेष्वसक्तात्मा विन्दत्यात्मनि यत्सुखम्। स ब्रह्मयोगयुक्तात्मा सुखमक्षयमश्नुते।।5.21।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: The joys that spring from external associations bring pain; they have their beginnings and their endings. The wise person does not rejoice in them.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: The joys that spring from external associations bring pain; they have their beginnings and their endings. The wise person does not rejoice in them.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ये हि संस्पर्शजा भोगा दुःखयोनय एव ते। आद्यन्तवन्तः कौन्तेय न तेषु रमते बुधः।।5.22।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He who, before leaving his body, learns to overcome the promptings of desire and anger, is a saint and is happy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He who, before leaving his body, learns to overcome the promptings of desire and anger, is a saint and is happy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात्। कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः।।5.23।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: He who is happy within himself and has found its peace, and in whom the inner light shines, that sage attains eternal bliss and becomes one with the spirit.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: He who is happy within himself and has found its peace, and in whom the inner light shines, that sage attains eternal bliss and becomes one with the spirit.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योऽन्तःसुखोऽन्तरारामस्तथान्तर्ज्योतिरेव यः। स योगी ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं ब्रह्मभूतोऽधिगच्छति।।5.24।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Sages whose sins have been washed away, whose sense of separateness has dissipated, who have subdued themselves, and seek only the welfare of all, come to the Eternal Spirit.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Sages whose sins have been washed away, whose sense of separateness has dissipated, who have subdued themselves, and seek only the welfare of all, come to the Eternal Spirit.
metadata.sanskrit_text: लभन्ते ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृषयः क्षीणकल्मषाः। छिन्नद्वैधा यतात्मानः सर्वभूतहिते रताः।।5.25।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Saints who know themselves, who control their minds, and feel neither desire nor anger, find eternal bliss everywhere.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Saints who know themselves, who control their minds, and feel neither desire nor anger, find eternal bliss everywhere.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कामक्रोधवियुक्तानां यतीनां यतचेतसाम्। अभितो ब्रह्मनिर्वाणं वर्तते विदितात्मनाम्।।5.26।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Excluding external objects, with his gaze fixed between the eyebrows, and the inward and outward breathings passing equally through his nostrils;
metadata.sanskrit_text: स्पर्शान्कृत्वा बहिर्बाह्यांश्चक्षुश्चैवान्तरे भ्रुवोः। प्राणापानौ समौ कृत्वा नासाभ्यन्तरचारिणौ।।5.27।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Governing sense, mind, and intellect, intent on liberation, free from desire, fear, and anger, the sage is eternally free.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Governing sense, mind, and intellect, intent on liberation, free from desire, fear, and anger, the sage is eternally free.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यतेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिर्मुनिर्मोक्षपरायणः। विगतेच्छाभयक्रोधो यः सदा मुक्त एव सः।।5.28।।

document:
Chapter: Karma Sanyasa Yoga
Meaning: Path of Renunciation
Translation: Knowing Me as the One who gladly receives all offerings of austerity and sacrifice, as the Mighty Ruler of all the Worlds and the Friend of all beings, he passes to Eternal Peace.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Renunciation
metadata.english_translation: Knowing Me as the One who gladly receives all offerings of austerity and sacrifice, as the Mighty Ruler of all the Worlds and the Friend of all beings, he passes to Eternal Peace.
metadata.sanskrit_text: भोक्तारं यज्ञतपसां सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम्। सुहृदं सर्वभूतानां ज्ञात्वा मां शान्तिमृच्छति।।5.29।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts out of duty, without considering the consequences, is truly spiritual and a true ascetic; not he who merely observes rituals or shuns all action.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts out of duty, without considering the consequences, is truly spiritual and a true ascetic; not he who merely observes rituals or shuns all action.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः। स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः।।6.1।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: O Arjuna, renunciation is indeed what is known as right action. No one can become spiritually enlightened who has not renounced all desires.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: O Arjuna, renunciation is indeed what is known as right action. No one can become spiritually enlightened who has not renounced all desires.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव। न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन।।6.2।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when they have attained it, they must maintain themselves there through continual self-control.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when they have attained it, they must maintain themselves there through continual self-control.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आरुरुक्षोर्मुनेर्योगं कर्म कारणमुच्यते। योगारूढस्य तस्यैव शमः कारणमुच्यते।।6.3।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, and is not interested in sense objects or any results that may flow from his acts, then he truly understands spirituality.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, and is not interested in sense objects or any results that may flow from his acts, then he truly understands spirituality.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा हि नेन्द्रियार्थेषु न कर्मस्वनुषज्जते। सर्वसङ्कल्पसंन्यासी योगारूढस्तदोच्यते।।6.4।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः।।6.5।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: To one who has conquered their lower nature with its help, the Self is a friend; but to one who has not done so, it is an enemy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: To one who has conquered their lower nature with its help, the Self is a friend; but to one who has not done so, it is an enemy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: बन्धुरात्माऽऽत्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः। अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्।।6.6।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: The Self of one who is self-controlled and has attained peace is equally unmoved by heat or cold, pleasure or pain, honor or dishonor.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: The Self of one who is self-controlled and has attained peace is equally unmoved by heat or cold, pleasure or pain, honor or dishonor.
metadata.sanskrit_text: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः। शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः।।6.7।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: He who desires nothing but wisdom and spiritual insight, who has conquered his senses, and who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone, and fine gold with the same eye, is a real saint.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: He who desires nothing but wisdom and spiritual insight, who has conquered his senses, and who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone, and fine gold with the same eye, is a real saint.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मा कूटस्थो विजितेन्द्रियः। युक्त इत्युच्यते योगी समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।।6.8।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: He looks impartially on all—lovers, friends, or foes; indifferent, hostile, alien, or relative; virtuous or sinful.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: He looks impartially on all—lovers, friends, or foes; indifferent, hostile, alien, or relative; virtuous or sinful.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सुहृन्मित्रार्युदासीनमध्यस्थद्वेष्यबन्धुषु। साधुष्वपि च पापेषु समबुद्धिर्विशिष्यते।।6.9।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with his mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with his mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.
metadata.sanskrit_text: योगी युञ्जीत सततमात्मानं रहसि स्थितः। एकाकी यतचित्तात्मा निराशीरपरिग्रहः।।6.10।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat that is neither too high nor too low, and cover it with a grass mat, a deer skin, and a cloth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat that is neither too high nor too low, and cover it with a grass mat, a deer skin, and a cloth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः। नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरम्।।6.11।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Seated thus, with his mind concentrated, his functions controlled, and his senses governed, let him practice meditation for the purification of his lower nature.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Seated thus, with his mind concentrated, his functions controlled, and his senses governed, let him practice meditation for the purification of his lower nature.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यतचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः। उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये।।6.12।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Let him hold his body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Let him hold his body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.
metadata.sanskrit_text: समं कायशिरोग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः। संप्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वं दिशश्चानवलोकयन्।।6.13।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: With peace in his heart and no fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with his mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: With peace in his heart and no fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with his mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रशान्तात्मा विगतभीर्ब्रह्मचारिव्रते स्थितः। मनः संयम्य मच्चित्तो युक्त आसीत मत्परः।।6.14।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Thus, keeping his mind always in communion with Me and subduing his thoughts, he shall attain that Peace which is Mine and will lead him to liberation at last.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Thus, keeping his mind always in communion with Me and subduing his thoughts, he shall attain that Peace which is Mine and will lead him to liberation at last.
metadata.sanskrit_text: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी नियतमानसः। शान्तिं निर्वाणपरमां मत्संस्थामधिगच्छति।।6.15।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, nor for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overly addicted to sleep, nor for him who is always awake.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, nor for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overly addicted to sleep, nor for him who is always awake.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः। न चातिस्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन।।6.16।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep, and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep, and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु। युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा।।6.17।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: When the mind is completely controlled, centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then the man is truly spiritual.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: When the mind is completely controlled, centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then the man is truly spiritual.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा विनियतं चित्तमात्मन्येवावतिष्ठते। निःस्पृहः सर्वकामेभ्यो युक्त इत्युच्यते तदा।।6.18।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता। योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः।।6.19।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: There, where the whole of nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the person abides within their Self and is satisfied there, their functions restrained by their union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: There, where the whole of nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the person abides within their Self and is satisfied there, their functions restrained by their union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्रोपरमते चित्तं निरुद्धं योगसेवया। यत्र चैवात्मनाऽऽत्मानं पश्यन्नात्मनि तुष्यति।।6.20।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: When he enjoys the bliss that surpasses the senses and can only be grasped by the pure intellect, when he comes to rest within his highest self, he will never again stray from reality.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: When he enjoys the bliss that surpasses the senses and can only be grasped by the pure intellect, when he comes to rest within his highest self, he will never again stray from reality.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सुखमात्यन्तिकं यत्तद्बुद्धिग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम्। वेत्ति यत्र न चैवायं स्थितश्चलति तत्त्वतः।।6.21।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Finding That, he will realize that there is no possession so precious. And once established there, no calamity can disturb him.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Finding That, he will realize that there is no possession so precious. And once established there, no calamity can disturb him.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यं लब्ध्वा चापरं लाभं मन्यते नाधिकं ततः। यस्मिन्स्थितो न दुःखेन गुरुणापि विचाल्यते।।6.22।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practiced with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practiced with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तं विद्याद् दुःखसंयोगवियोगं योगसंज्ञितम्। स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा।।6.23।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Renouncing every desire that can be imagined, controlling the senses at every point through the power of the mind;
metadata.sanskrit_text: सङ्कल्पप्रभवान्कामांस्त्यक्त्वा सर्वानशेषतः। मनसैवेन्द्रियग्रामं विनियम्य समन्ततः।।6.24।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Little by little, with the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Little by little, with the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.
metadata.sanskrit_text: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया। आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत्।।6.25।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम्। ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत्।।6.26।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Supreme bliss is the lot of the sage whose mind attains peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Supreme bliss is the lot of the sage whose mind attains peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रशान्तमनसं ह्येनं योगिनं सुखमुत्तमम्। उपैति शान्तरजसं ब्रह्मभूतमकल्मषम्।।6.27।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys, without effort, the bliss that flows from the realization of the Infinite.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys, without effort, the bliss that flows from the realization of the Infinite.
metadata.sanskrit_text: युञ्जन्नेवं सदाऽऽत्मानं योगी विगतकल्मषः। सुखेन ब्रह्मसंस्पर्शमत्यन्तं सुखमश्नुते।।6.28।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks upon everything with an impartial eye.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks upon everything with an impartial eye.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि। ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः।।6.29।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यो मां पश्यति सर्वत्र सर्वं च मयि पश्यति। तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति।।6.30।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: The sage who realizes the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, no matter what their lot may be.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: The sage who realizes the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, no matter what their lot may be.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वभूतस्थितं यो मां भजत्येकत्वमास्थितः। सर्वथा वर्तमानोऽपि स योगी मयि वर्तते।।6.31।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन। सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः।।6.32।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which You have revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which You have revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन। एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम्।।6.33।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.
metadata.sanskrit_text: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्। तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्।।6.34।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं। अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते।।6.35।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: It is not possible to attain Self-Realization unless one knows how to control oneself; however, for one who, striving by the proper means, learns such control, it is possible.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: It is not possible to attain Self-Realization unless one knows how to control oneself; however, for one who, striving by the proper means, learns such control, it is possible.
metadata.sanskrit_text: असंयतात्मना योगो दुष्प्राप इति मे मतिः। वश्यात्मना तु यतता शक्योऽवाप्तुमुपायतः।।6.36।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Arjuna asked: What of him who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, yet retains his faith and does not attain perfection?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked: What of him who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, yet retains his faith and does not attain perfection?
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः। अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति।।6.37।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Having failed in both, my Lord, is he without hope, like a riven cloud with no support, lost on the spiritual path?

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Having failed in both, my Lord, is he without hope, like a riven cloud with no support, lost on the spiritual path?
metadata.sanskrit_text: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति। अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि।।6.38।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: My Lord! You are worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; there is no one else competent to do so, save Yourself.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: My Lord! You are worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; there is no one else competent to do so, save Yourself.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एतन्मे संशयं कृष्ण छेत्तुमर्हस्यशेषतः। त्वदन्यः संशयस्यास्य छेत्ता न ह्युपपद्यते।।6.39।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते। नहि कल्याणकृत्कश्िचद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति।।6.40।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has strayed from the path of spirituality will be born again into the family of the pure, benevolent, and prosperous.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has strayed from the path of spirituality will be born again into the family of the pure, benevolent, and prosperous.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानुषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः। शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते।।6.41।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Or, he may be born in the family of wise sages, though such a birth is indeed very difficult to obtain.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Or, he may be born in the family of wise sages, though such a birth is indeed very difficult to obtain.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्। एतद्धि दुर्लभतरं लोके जन्म यदीदृशम्।।6.42।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Then, the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with it, he will more eagerly strive for perfection than before.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Then, the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with it, he will more eagerly strive for perfection than before.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्। यतते च ततो भूयः संसिद्धौ कुरुनन्दन।।6.43।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Unconsciously, he will return to the practices of his old life; thus, one who strives to attain spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who merely talks about it.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Unconsciously, he will return to the practices of his old life; thus, one who strives to attain spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who merely talks about it.
metadata.sanskrit_text: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः। जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते।।6.44।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: Then, after many lives of earnest striving and absolution of sins, the student of spirituality attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
metadata.english_translation: Then, after many lives of earnest striving and absolution of sins, the student of spirituality attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः। अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।6.45।।

document:
Chapter: Dhyana Yoga
Meaning: Path of Meditation
Translation: The wise person is superior to the ascetic, the scholar, and the man of action; therefore, be thou a wise person, O Arjuna!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Path of Meditation
