Translation: Darkness, stagnation, folly, and infatuation are the results of the dominance of ignorance, O joy of the Kuru clan!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Darkness, stagnation, folly, and infatuation are the results of the dominance of ignorance, O joy of the Kuru clan!
metadata.sanskrit_text: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च।तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन।।14.13।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: When purity prevails, the soul, upon leaving the body, passes on to the pure regions where those who know the Highest reside.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: When purity prevails, the soul, upon leaving the body, passes on to the pure regions where those who know the Highest reside.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत्।तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते।।14.14।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: When passion prevails, the soul is reborn among those who love activity; when ignorance rules, it enters the wombs of the ignorant.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: When passion prevails, the soul is reborn among those who love activity; when ignorance rules, it enters the wombs of the ignorant.
metadata.sanskrit_text: रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते।तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते।।14.15।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: They say the fruit of a meritorious action is spotless and pure; the outcome of passion is misery, and of ignorance, darkness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: They say the fruit of a meritorious action is spotless and pure; the outcome of passion is misery, and of ignorance, darkness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्मणः सुकृतस्याहुः सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम्।रजसस्तु फलं दुःखमज्ञानं तमसः फलम्।।14.16।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: Purity engenders wisdom, passion avarice, and ignorance folly, infatuation, and darkness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Purity engenders wisdom, passion avarice, and ignorance folly, infatuation, and darkness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च।प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च।।14.17।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: When purity is in the ascendant, the man evolves; when passion is in the ascendant, he neither evolves nor degenerates; when ignorance is in the ascendant, he is lost.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: When purity is in the ascendant, the man evolves; when passion is in the ascendant, he neither evolves nor degenerates; when ignorance is in the ascendant, he is lost.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसाः।जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसाः।।14.18।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: As soon as one understands that it is only the qualities that act and nothing else, and perceives that which is beyond, they attain My divine nature.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: As soon as one understands that it is only the qualities that act and nothing else, and perceives that which is beyond, they attain My divine nature.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नान्यं गुणेभ्यः कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति।गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति।।14.19।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: When the soul transcends the Qualities, which are the real cause of physical existence, then, freed from birth and death, from old age and misery, he drinks the nectar of immortality.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: When the soul transcends the Qualities, which are the real cause of physical existence, then, freed from birth and death, from old age and misery, he drinks the nectar of immortality.
metadata.sanskrit_text: गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान्।जन्ममृत्युजरादुःखैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्नुते।।14.20।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, how can one recognize someone who has transcended the qualities? How do they act and live beyond them?"

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, how can one recognize someone who has transcended the qualities? How do they act and live beyond them?"
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाचकैर्लिंगैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो।किमाचारः कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते।।14.21।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: O Prince! He who does not shun the quality that is present and does not long for that which is absent;
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाचप्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव।न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ्क्षति।।14.22।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: He who maintains an attitude of indifference, who is not disturbed by the qualities, who realizes that it is only they who act, and remains calm;
metadata.sanskrit_text: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते।गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते।।14.23।।

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Who accepts pain and pleasure as they come, is centered in their Self, to whom a piece of clay, stone, or gold are all the same, who neither likes nor dislikes, who is steadfast, indifferent alike to praise or censure;
metadata.sanskrit_text: समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः।तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः।।14.24।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: Who looks equally upon honor and dishonor, loves friends and foes alike, and abandons all initiative, such is he who transcends the qualities.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: Who looks equally upon honor and dishonor, loves friends and foes alike, and abandons all initiative, such is he who transcends the qualities.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः।सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते।।14.25।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: And he who serves Me alone, with unwavering devotion, shall overcome the Qualities and become one with the Eternal.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: And he who serves Me alone, with unwavering devotion, shall overcome the Qualities and become one with the Eternal.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्ितयोगेन सेवते।स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान् ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते।।14.26।।

document:
Chapter: Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
Translation: For I am the home of the spirit, the continual source of immortality, eternal righteousness, and infinite joy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
metadata.english_translation: For I am the home of the spirit, the continual source of immortality, eternal righteousness, and infinite joy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाऽहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च।शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च।।14.27।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna continued: This phenomenal creation, which is both ephemeral and eternal, is like a tree, with its seed above in the Highest and its ramifications below on this earth. The scriptures are its leaves, and he who understands this knows.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna continued: This phenomenal creation, which is both ephemeral and eternal, is like a tree, with its seed above in the Highest and its ramifications below on this earth. The scriptures are its leaves, and he who understands this knows.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्।।15.1।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Its branches shoot upwards and downwards, deriving their nourishment from the qualities; its buds are the objects of sense; and its roots, which follow the law, causing man's regeneration and degeneration, pierce downwards into the soil.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Its branches shoot upwards and downwards, deriving their nourishment from the qualities; its buds are the objects of sense; and its roots, which follow the law, causing man's regeneration and degeneration, pierce downwards into the soil.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः।अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके।।15.2।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: In this world, its true form is not known, neither its origin nor its end, and its strength is not understood—until the tree, with its roots striking deep into the earth, is hewn down by the sharp axe of non-attachment.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: In this world, its true form is not known, neither its origin nor its end, and its strength is not understood—until the tree, with its roots striking deep into the earth, is hewn down by the sharp axe of non-attachment.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा।अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा।।15.3।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Beyond lies the path, from which, once found, there is no return. This is the Primal God from whom this ancient creation has sprung.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Beyond lies the path, from which, once found, there is no return. This is the Primal God from whom this ancient creation has sprung.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः।तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी।।15.4।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: The wise attain Eternity when, freed from pride and delusion, they have conquered their love for the things of sense; when, renouncing desire and fixing their gaze on the Self, they cease to be tossed to and fro by the opposing sensations, such as pleasure and pain.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: The wise attain Eternity when, freed from pride and delusion, they have conquered their love for the things of sense; when, renouncing desire and fixing their gaze on the Self, they cease to be tossed to and fro by the opposing sensations, such as pleasure and pain.
metadata.sanskrit_text: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः।द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्।।15.5।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go there never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my celestial home!
metadata.sanskrit_text: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।।15.6।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: It is only a very small part of My Eternal Self, which is the life of the universe, that draws around itself the six senses, with the mind being the last, which have their source in Nature.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: It is only a very small part of My Eternal Self, which is the life of the universe, that draws around itself the six senses, with the mind being the last, which have their source in Nature.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः।मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति।।15.7।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: When the Supreme Lord enters a body or leaves it, He gathers these senses together and travels with them, as the wind gathers perfume while passing through the flowers.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: When the Supreme Lord enters a body or leaves it, He gathers these senses together and travels with them, as the wind gathers perfume while passing through the flowers.
metadata.sanskrit_text: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः।गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्।।15.8।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: He is the perception of the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste, the smell, and the mind; and the enjoyment of the things they perceive is also His.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: He is the perception of the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste, the smell, and the mind; and the enjoyment of the things they perceive is also His.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च।अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते।।15.9।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: The ignorant do not see that it is He who is present in life and departs at death, or even that it is He who enjoys pleasure through the qualities. Only the eye of wisdom sees this.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: The ignorant do not see that it is He who is present in life and departs at death, or even that it is He who enjoys pleasure through the qualities. Only the eye of wisdom sees this.
metadata.sanskrit_text: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम्।विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः।।15.10।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: The saints, with great effort, find Him within themselves; however, the unintelligent, despite their efforts, cannot control their minds.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: The saints, with great effort, find Him within themselves; however, the unintelligent, despite their efforts, cannot control their minds.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम्।यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः।।15.11।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Remember that the light which proceeds from the sun, illuminating the whole world, and the light which is in the moon, and that which is in the fire, all are born of me.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Remember that the light which proceeds from the sun, illuminating the whole world, and the light which is in the moon, and that which is in the fire, all are born of me.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम्।यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्।।15.12।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: I enter this world and animate all My creatures with My vitality; and by My cool moonbeams, I nourish the plants.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: I enter this world and animate all My creatures with My vitality; and by My cool moonbeams, I nourish the plants.
metadata.sanskrit_text: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा।पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः।।15.13।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Becoming the fire of life, I pass into their bodies and, uniting with the vital streams of Prāṇa and Apāna, I digest the various kinds of food.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Becoming the fire of life, I pass into their bodies and, uniting with the vital streams of Prāṇa and Apāna, I digest the various kinds of food.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः।प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्।।15.14।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: I am enthroned in the hearts of all; memory, wisdom, and discrimination owe their origins to Me. I am He Who is to be realized in the scriptures; I inspire their wisdom, and I know their truth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: I am enthroned in the hearts of all; memory, wisdom, and discrimination owe their origins to Me. I am He Who is to be realized in the scriptures; I inspire their wisdom, and I know their truth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च।वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्।।15.15।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: There are two aspects in Nature: the perishable and the imperishable. All life in this world belongs to the former, while the unchanging element belongs to the latter.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: There are two aspects in Nature: the perishable and the imperishable. All life in this world belongs to the former, while the unchanging element belongs to the latter.
metadata.sanskrit_text: द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च।क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते।।15.16।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: But I am higher than all, the Supreme God, the Absolute Self, the Eternal Lord, who pervades and upholds all the worlds.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: But I am higher than all, the Supreme God, the Absolute Self, the Eternal Lord, who pervades and upholds all the worlds.
metadata.sanskrit_text: उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः।यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः।।15.17।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: I am beyond comparison with the Eternal and the non-eternal; I am known as the Supreme Personality, the Highest God, by scriptures and sages.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: I am beyond comparison with the Eternal and the non-eternal; I am known as the Supreme Personality, the Highest God, by scriptures and sages.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः।अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः।।15.18।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: He who, with unclouded vision, sees Me as the Lord-God, knows all that there is to be known and will always worship Me with his whole heart.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: He who, with unclouded vision, sees Me as the Lord-God, knows all that there is to be known and will always worship Me with his whole heart.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम्।स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत।।15.19।।

document:
Chapter: Purushottama Yoga
Meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
Translation: Thus, O sinless one, I have revealed this most mystic knowledge to thee. He who understands it gains wisdom and attains the consummation of life.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
metadata.english_translation: Thus, O sinless one, I have revealed this most mystic knowledge to thee. He who understands it gains wisdom and attains the consummation of life.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयाऽनघ।एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत।।15.20।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna continued: Fearlessness, clean living, unceasing concentration on wisdom, readiness to give, self-control, a spirit of sacrifice, regular study of the scriptures, austerity, candor,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna continued: Fearlessness, clean living, unceasing concentration on wisdom, readiness to give, self-control, a spirit of sacrifice, regular study of the scriptures, austerity, candor,
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिः ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः। दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्।।16.1।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, contentment, straightforwardness, compassion towards all, uncovetousness, courtesy, modesty, and constancy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, contentment, straightforwardness, compassion towards all, uncovetousness, courtesy, modesty, and constancy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम्।दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्।।16.2।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Valor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from hate and vanity—these are the qualities of one who possesses the divine, O Arjuna!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Valor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from hate and vanity—these are the qualities of one who possesses the divine, O Arjuna!
metadata.sanskrit_text: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता। भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत।।16.3।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Hypocrisy, pride, insolence, cruelty, and ignorance belong to those born of godless qualities.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Hypocrisy, pride, insolence, cruelty, and ignorance belong to those born of godless qualities.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च।अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्।।16.4।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless ones lead to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! You have the Godly qualities.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Godly qualities lead to liberation; godless ones lead to bondage. Do not be anxious, Prince! You have the Godly qualities.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता।मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव।।16.5।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: No changes needed.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: No changes needed.
metadata.sanskrit_text: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च।दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे श्रृणु।।16.6।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: The godless do not know how to act or renounce; they lack both purity and truth. They do not understand the right principles of conduct.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: The godless do not know how to act or renounce; they lack both purity and truth. They do not understand the right principles of conduct.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः।न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते।।16.7।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: They say the universe is an accident with no purpose and no God. Life is created through sexual union, a product of lust and nothing else.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: They say the universe is an accident with no purpose and no God. Life is created through sexual union, a product of lust and nothing else.
metadata.sanskrit_text: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम्।अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्।।16.8।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Thinking thus, these degraded souls, these enemies of mankind—whose intelligence is negligible and whose deeds are monstrous—come into the world only to destroy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Thinking thus, these degraded souls, these enemies of mankind—whose intelligence is negligible and whose deeds are monstrous—come into the world only to destroy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः।प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः।।16.9।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Giving themselves up to insatiable passions, hypocritically, self-sufficiently, and arrogantly, cherishing false conceptions founded on delusion, they work only to carry out their own unholy purposes.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Giving themselves up to insatiable passions, hypocritically, self-sufficiently, and arrogantly, cherishing false conceptions founded on delusion, they work only to carry out their own unholy purposes.
metadata.sanskrit_text: काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः।मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः।।16.10।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Poring anxiously over evil resolutions that only end in death, seeking only the gratification of desire as the highest goal, and seeing nothing beyond—

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Poring anxiously over evil resolutions that only end in death, seeking only the gratification of desire as the highest goal, and seeing nothing beyond—
metadata.sanskrit_text: चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः।कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्िचताः।।16.11।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Caught in the toils of a hundred vain hopes, enslaved by passion and wrath, they accumulate hoards of unjust wealth, only to indulge their sensual desires.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Caught in the toils of a hundred vain hopes, enslaved by passion and wrath, they accumulate hoards of unjust wealth, only to indulge their sensual desires.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः।ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्।।16.12।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Today I have gained this; tomorrow I will fulfill another desire; this wealth is mine now, and the rest will soon be mine.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Today I have gained this; tomorrow I will fulfill another desire; this wealth is mine now, and the rest will soon be mine.
metadata.sanskrit_text: इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम्।इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्।।16.13।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: I have slain one enemy; I will slay the others too. I am worthy of enjoying; I am the Almighty, perfect, powerful, and happy.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: I have slain one enemy; I will slay the others too. I am worthy of enjoying; I am the Almighty, perfect, powerful, and happy.
metadata.sanskrit_text: असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि।ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी।।16.14।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: I am wealthy, I am of noble birth; who can compare with me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will pay—and I will enjoy. Thus blinded by ignorance,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: I am wealthy, I am of noble birth; who can compare with me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will pay—and I will enjoy. Thus blinded by ignorance,
metadata.sanskrit_text: आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया।यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः।।16.15।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Perplexed by discordant thoughts, entangled in the snares of desire, infatuated by passion, they sink into the depths of hell.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Perplexed by discordant thoughts, entangled in the snares of desire, infatuated by passion, they sink into the depths of hell.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः।प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ।।16.16।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, wealthy, proud, and insolent, they make a show of their patronage, disregarding the norms of propriety.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, wealthy, proud, and insolent, they make a show of their patronage, disregarding the norms of propriety.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः।यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम्।।16.17।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Puffed up by power and inordinate conceit, swayed by lust and wrath, these wicked people hate Me, Who am within them as I am within all.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Puffed up by power and inordinate conceit, swayed by lust and wrath, these wicked people hate Me, Who am within them as I am within all.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अहङ्कारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः।।16.18।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Those who thus hate Me, who are cruel, the dregs of mankind, I condemn them to a continuous, miserable, and godless rebirth.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Those who thus hate Me, who are cruel, the dregs of mankind, I condemn them to a continuous, miserable, and godless rebirth.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान्।क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु।।16.19।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: So, reborn, they spend life after life enveloped in delusion, and they never reach Me, O Prince, but degenerate into even lower forms of life.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: So, reborn, they spend life after life enveloped in delusion, and they never reach Me, O Prince, but degenerate into even lower forms of life.
metadata.sanskrit_text: असुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि।मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्।।16.20।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: The gates of hell are three: lust, wrath, and avarice; they destroy the Self, so avoid them.
metadata.sanskrit_text: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः।कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्।।16.21।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: These are the gates that lead to darkness; if one avoids them, they will ensure their own welfare and eventually attain liberation.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: These are the gates that lead to darkness; if one avoids them, they will ensure their own welfare and eventually attain liberation.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः।आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्।।16.22।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: But he who neglects the commands of the scriptures and follows the promptings of passion does not attain perfection, happiness, or the final goal.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: But he who neglects the commands of the scriptures and follows the promptings of passion does not attain perfection, happiness, or the final goal.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः।न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्।।16.23।।

document:
Chapter: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
Translation: Therefore, whenever there is doubt as to whether you should do something or not, let the scriptures guide your conduct. In the light of the scriptures, you should labor your whole life.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, whenever there is doubt as to whether you should do something or not, let the scriptures guide your conduct. In the light of the scriptures, you should labor your whole life.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ।ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि।।16.24।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is the condition of those who perform acts of sacrifice not according to the scriptures, but with implicit faith? Is it one of purity, passion, or ignorance?"

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is the condition of those who perform acts of sacrifice not according to the scriptures, but with implicit faith? Is it one of purity, passion, or ignorance?"
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाचये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयाऽन्विताः।तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः।।17.1।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Man has an inherent faith in one or another of the qualities—purity, passion, and ignorance. Now, listen.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Man has an inherent faith in one or another of the qualities—purity, passion, and ignorance. Now, listen.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाचत्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु।।17.2।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत।श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः।।17.3।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: The pure worship the true God; the passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the ignorant, the spirits of the dead and lower orders of nature.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: The pure worship the true God; the passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the ignorant, the spirits of the dead and lower orders of nature.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः।प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः।।17.4।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Those who practice austerities not commanded by scripture, who are enslaved to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Those who practice austerities not commanded by scripture, who are enslaved to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,
metadata.sanskrit_text: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः।।17.5।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: They are ignorant and torment the organs of the body, harassing Me who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: They are ignorant and torment the organs of the body, harassing Me who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः।मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्।।17.6।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: The food that people enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: The food that people enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः।यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं श्रृणु।।17.7।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: The foods that prolong life, increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness, and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial, and agreeable; these are loved by the pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: The foods that prolong life, increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness, and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial, and agreeable; these are loved by the pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः।रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः।।17.8।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Those in whom passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance, and disease.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Those in whom passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance, and disease.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः।आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः।।17.9।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: The ignorant love food that is stale, not nourishing, putrid, and corrupt; the leftovers of others, and unclean.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: The ignorant love food that is stale, not nourishing, putrid, and corrupt; the leftovers of others, and unclean.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्।।17.10।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Sacrifice is pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit of it, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Sacrifice is pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit of it, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते।यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः।।17.11।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्।।17.12।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith—that is the product of ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith—that is the product of ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम्।श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते।।17.13।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence, and harmlessness—all of these constitute physical austerity.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence, and harmlessness—all of these constitute physical austerity.
metadata.sanskrit_text: देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम्।ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते।।17.14।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते।।17.15।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity—these are the austerities of the mind.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity—these are the austerities of the mind.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः।भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते।।17.16।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: These threefold austerities, performed with faith and without thought of reward, can truly be considered pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: These threefold austerities, performed with faith and without thought of reward, can truly be considered pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्ित्रविधं नरैः।अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते।।17.17।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Austerity coupled with hypocrisy, or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity, or vanity, comes from passion, and its result is always uncertain and temporary.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Austerity coupled with hypocrisy, or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity, or vanity, comes from passion, and its result is always uncertain and temporary.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत्।क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्।।17.18।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or the infliction of pain upon oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or the infliction of pain upon oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः।परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।17.19।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: The gift that is given without thought of recompense, believing it should be made, in an appropriate place, at an opportune time, and to a deserving person—such a gift is pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: The gift that is given without thought of recompense, believing it should be made, in an appropriate place, at an opportune time, and to a deserving person—such a gift is pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे।देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्।।17.20।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense, or grudgingly—that may truly be said to be the outcome of passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense, or grudgingly—that may truly be said to be the outcome of passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः।दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्।।17.21।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: And that which is given at an inappropriate place or time or to one who is undeserving, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: And that which is given at an inappropriate place or time or to one who is undeserving, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते।असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।17.22।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which the Vedic Scriptures, ceremonials, and sacrifices were ordained of old.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which the Vedic Scriptures, ceremonials, and sacrifices were ordained of old.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः।ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा।।17.23।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Therefore, all acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities prescribed by the scriptures are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word "Om."

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Therefore, all acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities prescribed by the scriptures are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word "Om."
metadata.sanskrit_text: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः।प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्।।17.24।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity, or gift with the word "Tat" (meaning "That"), without thought of reward.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity, or gift with the word "Tat" (meaning "That"), without thought of reward.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः।दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षि।।17.25।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to denote an action of exceptional merit.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to denote an action of exceptional merit.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते।प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते।।17.26।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Conviction in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called Sat. So too, an action done only for the Lord's sake.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Conviction in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called Sat. So too, an action done only for the Lord's sake.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते।।17.27।।

document:
Chapter: Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
Translation: Whatever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity, gift, or anything else, is called Asat (meaning "Unreal"), for it is the negation of Sat, O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
metadata.english_translation: Whatever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity, gift, or anything else, is called Asat (meaning "Unreal"), for it is the negation of Sat, O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह।।17.28।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Arjuna asked, "O Mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Arjuna asked, "O Mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अर्जुन उवाच संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम्। त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन।।18.1।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.
metadata.sanskrit_text: श्री भगवानुवाच काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः। सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः।।18.2।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Some philosophers say that all action is evil and should be abandoned, whereas others maintain that acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Some philosophers say that all action is evil and should be abandoned, whereas others maintain that acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up.
metadata.sanskrit_text: त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः। यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे।।18.3।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment regarding this problem. It has a threefold aspect.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment regarding this problem. It has a threefold aspect.
metadata.sanskrit_text: निश्चयं श्रृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम।त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः संप्रकीर्तितः।।18.4।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up, but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up, but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत्।यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्।।18.5।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But they should be done with detachment and without thought of reward. This is my final judgement.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But they should be done with detachment and without thought of reward. This is my final judgement.
metadata.sanskrit_text: एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च।कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्िचतं मतमुत्तमम्।।18.6।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: It is not right to give up actions which are obligatory; and if they are misunderstood, it is the result of sheer ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: It is not right to give up actions which are obligatory; and if they are misunderstood, it is the result of sheer ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते।मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.7।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: To avoid an action out of fear of physical suffering, as it is likely to be painful, is to act out of passion, and the benefit of renunciation will not be gained.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: To avoid an action out of fear of physical suffering, as it is likely to be painful, is to act out of passion, and the benefit of renunciation will not be gained.
metadata.sanskrit_text: दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत्।स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्।।18.8।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: He who performs an obligatory action, believing it to be a duty that ought to be done, without any personal desire to do the act or to receive any return—such renunciation is pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: He who performs an obligatory action, believing it to be a duty that ought to be done, without any personal desire to do the act or to receive any return—such renunciation is pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन।सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलं चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः।।18.9।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The wise man who has attained purity, whose doubts are resolved, who is filled with the spirit of self-abnegation, does not shy away from action due to its pain, nor does he crave it due to its pleasure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The wise man who has attained purity, whose doubts are resolved, who is filled with the spirit of self-abnegation, does not shy away from action due to its pain, nor does he crave it due to its pleasure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते।त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः।।18.10।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But since those still in the body cannot entirely avoid action, in their case, the abandonment of the fruit of action is considered as complete renunciation.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But since those still in the body cannot entirely avoid action, in their case, the abandonment of the fruit of action is considered as complete renunciation.
metadata.sanskrit_text: न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः।यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते।।18.11।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: For those who cannot renounce all desires, the fruit of action hereafter is threefold—good, evil, and partly good and partly evil. But for him who has renounced, there is none.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: For those who cannot renounce all desires, the fruit of action hereafter is threefold—good, evil, and partly good and partly evil. But for him who has renounced, there is none.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम्।भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्।।18.12।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: I will now tell you, O Mighty Man, the five causes that must come together, according to the final decision of philosophy, for an action to be accomplished.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: I will now tell you, O Mighty Man, the five causes that must come together, according to the final decision of philosophy, for an action to be accomplished.
metadata.sanskrit_text: पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे।सांख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्।।18.13।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: They have a body, a personality, physical organs, and manifold activities and destinies.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: They have a body, a personality, physical organs, and manifold activities and destinies.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम्।विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्।।18.14।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Whatever action a person performs, whether by muscular effort, speech, or thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Whatever action a person performs, whether by muscular effort, speech, or thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.
metadata.sanskrit_text: शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः।न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः।।18.15।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But the fool, who, due to his immature judgment, supposes that it is his own Self alone that acts, perverts the truth and does not see rightly.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But the fool, who, due to his immature judgment, supposes that it is his own Self alone that acts, perverts the truth and does not see rightly.
metadata.sanskrit_text: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः।पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः।।18.16।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: He who has no pride and whose intellect is unalloyed by attachment, even though he kills these people, he does not kill them, and his act does not bind him.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: He who has no pride and whose intellect is unalloyed by attachment, even though he kills these people, he does not kill them, and his act does not bind him.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यस्य नाहंकृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते।हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते।।18.17।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge are the three incentives to action; and the act, the actor, and the instrument are the threefold constituents.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge are the three incentives to action; and the act, the actor, and the instrument are the threefold constituents.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना।करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः।।18.18।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The knowledge, the action, and the doer differ according to their qualities. Listen to this as well.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The knowledge, the action, and the doer differ according to their qualities. Listen to this as well.
metadata.sanskrit_text: ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः।प्रोच्यते गुणसंख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि।।18.19।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, can be truly called Pure Knowledge.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, can be truly called Pure Knowledge.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते।अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्।।18.20।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The knowledge that perceives the manifold existence in all beings as separate comes from passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The knowledge that perceives the manifold existence in all beings as separate comes from passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान्।वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्।।18.21।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth, or insight, has its origin in darkness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth, or insight, has its origin in darkness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम्।अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्।।18.22।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that may follow, such an action is Pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that may follow, such an action is Pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम्।अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते।।18.23।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But even though an action involves the most strenuous endeavor, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify their desires and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But even though an action involves the most strenuous endeavor, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify their desires and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः।क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्।।18.24।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: An action undertaken through delusion, with no regard to the spiritual implications, the capacity of the doer, or the potential harm that may follow, is assumed to be a product of ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: An action undertaken through delusion, with no regard to the spiritual implications, the capacity of the doer, or the potential harm that may follow, is assumed to be a product of ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम्।मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते।।18.25।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: But when a person has no sentiment or ego, when they possess courage and confidence, not caring whether they succeed or fail, then their action arises from purity.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: But when a person has no sentiment or ego, when they possess courage and confidence, not caring whether they succeed or fail, then their action arises from purity.
metadata.sanskrit_text: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः।सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते।।18.26।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: In one who is impulsive, greedy, looking for reward, violent, impure, and torn between joy and sorrow, it may be assumed that Passion is predominant.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: In one who is impulsive, greedy, looking for reward, violent, impure, and torn between joy and sorrow, it may be assumed that Passion is predominant.
metadata.sanskrit_text: रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः।हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः।।18.27।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: While he whose purpose is weak, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—he may be assumed to be in darkness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: While he whose purpose is weak, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—he may be assumed to be in darkness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः।विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते।।18.28।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the quality that is dominant. I will explain them fully and separately, O Arjuna!

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the quality that is dominant. I will explain them fully and separately, O Arjuna!
metadata.sanskrit_text: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं श्रृणु।प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय।।18.29।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is Pure.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is Pure.
metadata.sanskrit_text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये।बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.30।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The intellect that does not understand what is right and wrong, and what should be done and not done, is under the sway of Passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The intellect that does not understand what is right and wrong, and what should be done and not done, is under the sway of Passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च।अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी।।18.31।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong to be right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong to be right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.
metadata.sanskrit_text: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसाऽऽवृता।सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.32।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The conviction and steady concentration with which the mind, the energy, and the senses are controlled—O Arjuna!—are the result of purity.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The conviction and steady concentration with which the mind, the energy, and the senses are controlled—O Arjuna!—are the result of purity.
metadata.sanskrit_text: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः।योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी।।18.33।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: The conviction that always holds fast to rituals, self-interest, and wealth for the sake of what they may bring forth comes from passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: The conviction that always holds fast to rituals, self-interest, and wealth for the sake of what they may bring forth comes from passion.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान् धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन।प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी।।18.34।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: And that which clings perversely to false idealism, fear, grief, despair, and vanity is the product of ignorance.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: And that which clings perversely to false idealism, fear, grief, despair, and vanity is the product of ignorance.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च।न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी।।18.35।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Hear further the three kinds of pleasure. That which increases day by day delivers one from misery.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Hear further the three kinds of pleasure. That which increases day by day delivers one from misery.
metadata.sanskrit_text: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं श्रृणु मे भरतर्षभ।अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति।।18.36।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: Which at first seems like poison but afterwards acts like nectar—that pleasure is pure, for it is born of wisdom.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: Which at first seems like poison but afterwards acts like nectar—that pleasure is pure, for it is born of wisdom.
metadata.sanskrit_text: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम्।तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्।।18.37।।

document:
Chapter: Moksha Sanyaas Yoga
Meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
Translation: That which, at first, is like nectar, as the senses revel in their objects, but in the end acts like poison—that pleasure arises from Passion.

metadata.chapter_title_meaning: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
metadata.english_translation: That which, at first, is like nectar, as the senses revel in their objects, but in the end acts like poison—that pleasure arises from Passion.
